### Observed differences

- In the later window, A12 appears in about 32 in 100 traces, up from about 24 in 100 (63 vs 49 of 200 traces), and its successor mix changed markedly: A03 now follows A12 in about 43% of A12's outgoing transitions (previously 24%) and A06 in about 17% (previously 2%), while A01, A09 and A10 as successors fell to about 3%, 8% and 11% (previously 14%, 16% and 20%); this difference is larger than in about 98 in 100 random re-splits of these windows. [OCC012, DIR012]
- Participation swapped between A01 and A06: A01 appears in about 46 in 100 later traces versus about 54 earlier (93 vs 107 traces), while A06 appears in about 54 versus about 46 (107 vs 93); each difference is larger than in about 79 in 100 random re-splits. [OCC001, OCC006]
- A01 now leads to A04 in only about 4% of its outgoing transitions (previously 13%) and more often to A12 (about 13% vs 9%); A04 itself appears in about 22 in 100 traces (previously 27; 45 vs 54 traces) and leads to A03 in about 24% of its outgoing transitions (previously 41%), while A06 as its successor rose to about 16% (previously 7%). [DIR001, OCC004, DIR004]
- A06's outgoing mix moved toward A03 and A09 (each about 13%, previously 7.5%) and away from A02 (about 25% vs 32%) and A10 (about 18% vs 23%); A10 in turn leads to A12 about three times as often as before (about 11% vs 3.5% of its outgoing transitions). [DIR006, DIR010]
- Apart from A01, A04, A06 and A12, all participations moved by at most about 3 points (mostly under 1), and the outgoing profiles of the other source activities changed only marginally, so the differences are localised to these four activities and their immediate continuations. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC013, OCC014, DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR013]
- Two small shifts fall outside this pattern: A14 is now followed by A11 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 91), and A11's outgoing moved from A02 (about 11% vs 21%) toward A09 (about 28% vs 21%), the latter based on only about 19 and 18 outgoing transitions. [DIR014, DIR011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a routing shift in the middle of the process: in the later window a larger share of cases runs through A12 and A06 and a smaller share through A01 and A04, with A12 now more often followed by A03 or A06 and A04 less often followed by A03. Supporting signs are the exactly mirrored participation swap between A01 and A06 (A01 lost 14 traces while A06 gained 14, and A12 gained the same 14), A12's rise combined with the largest and least chance-like successor redistribution in the evidence, A04's decline accompanied by its outgoing shift away from A03 toward A06, and A10 leading to A12 about three times as often; occurrence and directional indicators agree on the same activities while the rest of the process stayed flat. [OCC012, DIR012, OCC001, OCC006, OCC004, DIR001, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010]

The main limitation is that the evidence contains no relational items, so it cannot show that the same cases switched from an A01/A04 route to an A12/A06 route; that link is inferred from agreeing aggregate shifts rather than observed directly. The A04 changes rest on few outgoing transitions (54 vs 45), and several supporting items show only moderate empirical strength (larger than in roughly 34–65 in 100 random re-splits), so sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows remains a competing explanation for those weaker components. [OCC004, DIR004, DIR001, DIR006, DIR010]

Other differences: A14 is now followed by A11 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 91), and A11's own outgoing shifted from A02 toward A09, though the latter rests on roughly 19 and 18 transitions; these involve activities outside the routing shift above. [DIR014, DIR011]
